verdict.rationale: The axis applies, since an auth service could plausibly act as an OAuth/OIDC provider, but the evidence pack shows no such capability. The evidence covers Supabase consuming external OAuth providers (social login, custom OAuth/OIDC providers, third-party JWTs) and exposing a JWKS URL for its own tokens. These are adjacent features, not issuing tokens to third-party clients. One community user wants to use Supabase Auth as an IdP and is building that on top of it themselves, which is a user-side workaround and earns no credit.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn my own application into an OAuth provider that issues tokens to third-party clients ("Sign in with my app")
